'''Stephen S. Kudla''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC}} (born 1950 Caracas, Venezuela<ref>A Community of Scholars, The Institute for Advanced Study, Faculty and Members 1930–1980 [https://library.ias.edu/files/pdfs/hs/cos.pdf]</ref>) is an American mathematician working in [[arithmetic geometry]] and [[automorphic form]]s.  He is a professor in the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of Toronto]].<ref>[https://www.math.toronto.edu/cms/kudla-stephen/ Kudla, Stephen » Department of Mathematics]</ref><ref>[http://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileId=2300 Canada Research Chair – Stephen Kudla]</ref>

==Life==
{{BLP sources section|date=November 2017}}
After receiving his doctorate, Kudla spent a year at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton, following which he joined the faculty at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]].<ref>[http://www.pims.math.ca/pims-glance/scientific-review-panel/past-members Pacific Institute for the Mathematical Sciences, Past Members]</ref> Since 2006, he has been a  professor at the [[University of Toronto]] where he held a [[Canada Research Chair]] for the period 2006–2020.

In 1997, he discovered relationships between the Fourier coefficients of derivatives of [[Siegel Eisenstein series]] and arithmetic invariants of [[Shimura variety|Shimura varieties]] (heights pairings of arithmetic cycles).<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Kudla|first1=Stephen S.|title=Central Derivatives of Eisenstein Series and Height Pairings|journal=Annals of Mathematics|date=1997|volume=146|issue=3|pages=545–646|doi=10.2307/2952456|jstor=2952456}}</ref>

He was a [[Sloan Fellow]] in 1981, received the Max-Planck Research Award in 2000, and the [[Jeffery–Williams Prize]] of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] in 2009. He was an Invited Speaker at the 2002 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Beijing, where he gave a lecture on "Derivatives of Eisenstein series and arithmetic geometry". He was on the Scientific Review Panel of the [[Pacific Institute for the Mathematical Sciences]] (PIMS) for the period 2009–2013. For 2004 - 2010, he was a co-editor of the [[Canadian Journal of Mathematics]], and has been co-organizer of several conferences at the [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach]].

==Education==
*Ph.D. [[Stony Brook University|State University of New York at Stony Brook]] 1975; Dissertation: Real Points on Algebraic Varieties Defined by Quaternion Algebras. Advisor: [[Michio Kuga]].<ref>[https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=1117 The Mathematics Genealogy Project – Stephen Kudla]</ref>
